A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CogAlign research. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, two tables, six figures and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic evaluations across five datasets, single-label and multi-label results, robustness tests, masking comparisons, ablations and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations and their reported outcomes in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: Both versions retain hierarchical clinical-cognition SFT followed by counterfactual-driven GRPO, Gaussian lesion masking, and the same format, nine-keyword cognition and diagnostic rewards. No algorithmic component, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both use CrohnIPI, GastroVision, HyperKvasir, Kvasir-Capsule and The SEE-AI Project, retaining single-label diagnosis, concurrent-pathology diagnosis and spot-interference testing. Revised collection wording does not establish different represented data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same 15 comparator rows: Gemini, GPT-5, Qwen3-VL, Hulu-Med and internal SFT variants. The Qwen3-VL-Plus and Base-SFT-8B case-study comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The 19,736/4,779 training/test split, 235 multi-label test cases, accuracy and exact-label-set scoring, model scales, and 400-step SFT/200-step GRPO budgets remain unchanged. Removed implementation disclosures do not establish changed experimental conditions.

E4.justification: Both retain the polyp and erosion cases, spot-interference robustness test, Gaussian-versus-white masking comparison, and SFT/cognition-reward/diagnostic-reward ablations. Shortened descriptions and captions do not change the analyses performed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The unchanged G=8 setting concerns GRPO response sampling, rather than repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1–2 is retained. For example, CogAlign-8B remains at 67.67% overall accuracy and 13.62% multi-label accuracy. The case-study outcomes and robustness, masking and ablation plots also retain their results.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–2, both shortcut-convergence and causal-rectification theorems, and their proofs retain the same mathematical content. Shortening Section 4.3's heading and removing redundant intervention notation from explanatory prose do not revise the formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of hierarchical clinical reasoning alignment, counterfactual causal rectification, a new cognition dataset and state-of-the-art diagnostic performance. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The implementation discussion removes the explicit rationale that freezing the vision encoder and aligner preserves foundational perception. The main explanations of multi-label performance, robustness and masking remain, with no new substantive limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 removes disclosures of bfloat16 precision, Flash Attention, the 450,560-pixel image cap, shared baseline prompts/protocols, and the planned public release of code and datasets. Section 3.2 and Figure 2 also revise collection documentation from web search/crawling toward public datasets/formatting. Most hardware and optimization details remain; actual resource withdrawal or experimental reruns are not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds ten cited works, including adaptive causal reasoning, MedEyes, MedSynapse-V and continual vision-language learning papers, and removes the MedGemma technical report. These mainly expand citation lists within retained introductory and related-work arguments, without substantially redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 shortens prose across several sections, corrects Experiment Setup from a separate Section 6 to Section 5.1, and adds an equal-contribution author note. The overall narrative and substantive section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives revised panel framing and collection labels; Figure 3 is enlarged. Tables 1–2 extend green highlighting across the proposed-model group, several captions are shortened, and displays shift with text reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves section organization and makes modest presentation refinements, but removes useful reproducibility disclosures, especially numerical precision, attention implementation, image resolution and baseline evaluation consistency. It also drops the code/data-release commitment. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these concrete transparency losses outweigh the limited editorial gains.
